en: ship's captain; commander of a warship

examples.en: The captain gave an order to all the crew.
I thought the captain role I saw in the movie was cool.

examples.ko: 함장은 배가 안전하게 항구에 닿을 때까지 자리를 지켰어요.
examples.en: The captain stayed at his post until the ship safely reached port.
My grandfather was a navy captain when he was young.
Captain, I see a large ship ahead!

examples.ko: 새로 온 함장은 승무원들과 먼저 인사를 나눴어요.
examples.en: The newly arrived captain first greeted the crew.

explain: 함장은 군함의 가장 높은 책임자예요. 일반 배나 여객선의 책임자는 '선장'이라고 해요. 비행기는 '기장'이고 잠수함도 '함장'을 써요.

phrases.en: The captain came out onto the deck.
phrases.nuance_ko: '함장'을 높여 부르거나 직접 부를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form of 함장, used to address or refer to the captain respectfully.

phrases.en: He is a submarine captain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함장이 어떤 배의 책임자인지 밝힐 때 앞에 배 이름을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the type of vessel before 함장 shows which ship the captain commands.

phrases.example: 그는 십 년 뒤에 함장이 됐어요.
phrases.en: Ten years later, he became a captain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군함의 책임자 자리에 오르는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for rising to the position of commanding a warship.

explain_en: A 함장 is the commanding officer of a warship. The person in charge of an ordinary ship or ferry is a 선장, and for an airplane it is 기장. Submarines also use 함장.

examples.en: He was a professor and then came to work as an administrator.

examples.ko: 좋은 행정가는 시민의 말을 잘 들어요.
examples.en: A good administrator listens well to citizens.

examples.ko: 시장은 오랫동안 일한 행정가를 새 부시장으로 뽑았어요.
examples.en: The mayor chose a long-serving administrator as the new deputy mayor.
My father was an administrator who worked at city hall.

examples.ko: 학자와 행정가의 생각은 서로 다를 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Scholars and administrators often think differently.

examples.ko: 저는 나중에 행정가가 되어 지역을 돕고 싶어요.
examples.en: Later I want to become an administrator and help my region.

explain: '정치가'는 선거나 정당 활동으로 정치를 하는 사람이고, '행정가'는 정책을 실제로 실행하고 조직을 운영하는 사람이에요. 공무원 전체를 부를 때는 보통 '공무원'이라고 하고, '행정가'는 능력이나 경력을 이야기할 때 써요.

phrases.en: He is known as a capable administrator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력을 칭찬할 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing used to praise someone's ability.

phrases.example: 새 시장은 행정가 출신이라서 일 처리가 빨라요.
phrases.en: The new mayor comes from an administrative background, so he gets things done quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 사람의 경력이 행정 분야임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone's career background is in administration.

phrases.en: As an administrator, you have to work with a sense of responsibility.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자격이나 입장을 나타낼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state someone's role or standpoint.

explain_en: A '정치가' (politician) works in politics through elections or parties, while a '행정가' runs organizations and carries out policy. For public workers in general people usually say '공무원'; '행정가' is used when talking about someone's ability or career.

en: on intimate terms with; without reserve; candidly

examples.en: The staff treat the regular customer in a very friendly way.

examples.ko: 선배가 허물없이 말을 걸어 줘서 편했어요.
examples.en: The senior talked to me so casually that I felt at ease.
We are on very easy, intimate terms with each other.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 누구에게나 허물없이 웃으며 인사해요.
examples.en: That person greets everyone with a warm, open smile.
If you have a worry, please tell me freely.

examples.ko: 처음 보는 사람과도 허물없이 어울리는 게 신기해요.
examples.en: It is amazing how you mix easily even with people you have just met.

explain: '허물없이 대하다·지내다·이야기하다·어울리다'처럼 사람과 관계를 맺는 동사와 함께 써요. 격식 없이 마음을 터놓는 따뜻한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: We have been on easy, close terms for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이가 가깝고 편하게 지낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for being on close and comfortable terms.

phrases.en: Talking openly with a friend puts my mind at ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨기는 것 없이 편하게 말한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means talking freely without holding anything back.

phrases.en: All the neighbors mingle easily with one another.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 거리낌 없이 함께 지낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people get along together without reserve.

explain_en: It pairs with verbs about relating to people, such as '허물없이 대하다/지내다/이야기하다/어울리다'. It carries a warm feeling of being open and unceremonious.

examples.en: Grandfather shouted orders at the children in a loud voice.
The commander barks at the soldiers to move forward.

examples.ko: 사장님이 직원들을 호령하듯 말해서 분위기가 무거워졌어요.
examples.en: The boss spoke as if giving orders to the staff, and the mood became heavy.

examples.ko: 그는 이 동네를 호령하던 유명한 사람이었어요.
examples.en: He was a famous man who used to rule this neighborhood.

examples.ko: 왕이 신하들에게 호령하는 장면이 드라마에 나와요.
examples.en: There is a scene in the drama where the king shouts orders at his subjects.

examples.ko: 그렇게 호령하지 말고 부드럽게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't bark orders like that; speak gently.

explain: 힘 있는 사람이 크고 위엄 있게 명령하는 모습에 써요. 화가 나서 크게 야단치는 '호통치다'와 비슷하지만, '호령하다'는 명령하거나 다스리는 느낌이 더 강해요. 사극이나 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 일상에서는 비유로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The general commanded the soldiers in a loud voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위엄 있게 크게 명령하는 모습에 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for commanding loudly and with authority.

phrases.en: That king once ruled over the whole land.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 힘을 가지고 다스리는 모습을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for ruling with great power.

phrases.en: The father scolded his son loudly for coming home late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화가 나서 크게 야단치는 말로, '호령하다'는 명령하는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means scolding loudly out of anger; 호령하다 has more of a commanding feel.

explain_en: It describes a powerful person giving orders in a loud, commanding way. It is close to '호통치다' (to scold loudly), but '호령하다' feels more like commanding or ruling. It often appears in historical dramas and stories, and in daily life it is sometimes used figuratively.

en: to be promoted; to be elevated

examples.ko: 지진 이후 경보 단계가 한 단계 격상됐어요.
examples.en: After the earthquake, the alert level was raised by one step.
This town will be upgraded to a city starting next year.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 본부로 격상되면서 인원도 늘었어요.
examples.en: As our team was upgraded to a division, the staff increased too.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 동맹으로 격상된다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that the relationship between the two countries is being raised to an alliance.

examples.ko: 행사 규모가 커지면서 대회 등급이 격상될 예정이에요.
examples.en: As the event grows, the competition's grade is set to be raised.

examples.ko: 위기 단계가 격상되자 학교가 모두 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: When the crisis level was raised, all the schools closed.

explain: 등급, 지위, 단계, 관계가 위로 올라갈 때 쓰고, 뉴스에서 '경보 단계가 격상되다'처럼 자주 나와요. 반대말은 '격하되다'예요. 사람의 직급이 오르는 건 보통 '승진하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The typhoon warning was raised by one level.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경보나 등급이 위로 올라갈 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news when a warning or grade goes up.

phrases.example: 이 지역은 내년에 시로 격상될 예정이에요.
phrases.en: This area is scheduled to be elevated to a city next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 지위가 올라갈 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a planned future rise in status.

phrases.en: The danger level was lowered again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '격상되다'의 반대말로, 등급이나 지위가 내려갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 격상되다, used when a level or status goes down.

explain_en: It is used when a grade, status, level or relationship goes up, and it often appears in the news, as in '경보 단계가 격상되다'. Its opposite is '격하되다'. When a person moves up in rank, people usually say '승진하다'.

examples.en: He holds both the professor and institute director positions.

examples.ko: 팀장이 인사 업무까지 겸임해서 많이 바빠요.
examples.en: The team leader also handles HR duties, so he is very busy.

examples.ko: 한 사람이 두 자리를 겸임하기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy for one person to hold two posts at once.
The new president will also serve as chairman of the board.

examples.ko: 두 부서의 일을 겸임하는 직원이 늘었어요.
examples.en: The number of employees working in two departments at once has grown.
The CEO decided not to hold the director post at the same time.

explain: 한 사람이 원래 맡은 직책 말고 다른 직책이나 업무를 함께 맡을 때 써요. 회사, 학교, 정부 인사 소식에 자주 나와요. '겸직'도 비슷한 뜻으로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '같이 맡다'라고 풀어서 말해요.

phrases.en: That doctor holds both hospital director and professor positions.
phrases.nuance_ko: '겸임하다'와 비슷한 뜻이고 직업이나 직책 이야기에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 겸임하다, used for jobs and positions.
phrases.en_equiv: to hold two jobs at once

phrases.en: I work as an adjunct professor at a university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 일을 하면서 학교에서도 가르치는 교수를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The term for a professor who teaches at a school while also holding another job.

phrases.example: 다음 달부터 제가 홍보 업무를 겸임하게 됐어요.
phrases.en: From next month I will also be in charge of public relations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로운 일을 함께 맡게 되었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you have come to take on an additional duty.
phrases.en_equiv: to end up holding another post as well

explain_en: It is used when one person takes on another post or duty in addition to their main one. It often appears in personnel news from companies, schools and the government. '겸직' is used with a similar meaning, and in daily talk people say '같이 맡다'.

examples.en: A rank badge is attached to the shoulder of the uniform.
My father polished his rank badge until it shone.
This badge means the rank of sergeant.
Let's talk comfortably today without pulling rank.
Rank badges are attached to police uniforms too.
Judging by the badges, he is the highest in rank.

explain: 군복이나 경찰·소방 제복에 달아서 계급을 나타내는 표예요. 비유로 '계급장 떼고'라고 하면 직급이나 나이를 따지지 않는다는 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 계급장 떼고 솔직하게 말해 봐요.
phrases.en: without pulling rank
phrases.nuance_ko: 직급이나 나이 같은 위아래 관계를 접어 두고 대등하게 이야기하자고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when proposing to set aside hierarchy such as job title or age and talk as equals.
phrases.en_equiv: drop the titles and speak as equals

explain_en: It is a badge worn on military, police or fire-service uniforms to show rank. Figuratively, '계급장 떼고' means setting aside rank or age and speaking as equals.

examples.en: He ended up rising to a senior government post.
Senior civil servants must disclose their assets.

examples.ko: 고위직에 있는 사람일수록 말을 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The higher someone's position, the more careful they must be with their words.
My uncle works in a senior position at a bank.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 여성 고위직이 많지 않아요.
examples.en: This company doesn't have many women in senior positions.
The senior appointments were announced this morning.

explain: '고위직'은 회사나 정부의 높은 자리를 통틀어 부를 때 쓰고 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 구체적인 자리는 '장관', '임원'처럼 따로 이름이 있고 고위직은 그런 자리들의 묶음 이름이에요. 반대는 '하위직'이에요.

phrases.en: He worked hard and rose to a high position.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 자리까지 올라갔다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means someone climbed up to a high position.
phrases.en_equiv: to rise to a high position

phrases.en: He holds a high-ranking position at the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 그 자리에서 일하고 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means he currently works in that position.

phrases.en: The high-level personnel appointments will be announced tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 자리의 사람을 새로 정하는 일로, 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means choosing people for top positions and is common in the news.

explain_en: 고위직 is a collective name for high positions in companies or the government, and it appears often in the news. Specific posts have their own names like 장관 and 임원, and 고위직 groups them together. The opposite is 하위직.

en: to oversee; to supervise; to be in charge of

examples.en: This department oversees the school events.
City Hall is in charge of the city's traffic.
The director oversees the entire hospital.
Do you know who is in charge of this?

examples.ko: 한 사람이 모든 업무를 관장하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard for one person to oversee all the work.
That committee was in charge of writing the exam.

explain: 기관이나 높은 자리의 사람이 어떤 일을 책임지고 맡을 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. '담당하다'는 실무를 맡는 느낌이고, '관장하다'는 전체를 총괄하는 느낌이에요. 뉴스와 공문에서 주로 보고, 일상 대화에서는 '맡다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Which department oversees education?
phrases.nuance_ko: '관장하는'은 명사 앞에서 책임지는 기관을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: '관장하는' modifies a noun to name the body in charge.

phrases.en: I am in charge of this work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 일을 맡는 느낌이고 '관장하다'보다 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests handling the actual work, and is more everyday than '관장하다'.

phrases.en: I'm taking charge of preparing the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 자연스러운 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest and most natural word in daily conversation.

explain_en: It is a formal word used when an organization or a person in a high position takes responsibility for a whole area of work. 담당하다 feels like handling the practical tasks, while 관장하다 feels like overseeing everything. You mostly see it in news and official documents; in daily talk people say 맡다.

dis.h: formal; hold authority over a whole field
gh: run a business as an owner or boss
look after and keep in good condition
literary; carry on a business or a life

p.n: 관리 means handle or maintain the work; 관장 means being in charge of the whole area.

examples.en: The coach used the rookie as a starter.

examples.ko: 새 대표는 젊은 인재를 적극적으로 기용하고 있어요.
examples.en: The new CEO is actively appointing young talent.

examples.ko: 회사에서 외부 전문가를 팀장으로 기용하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to appoint an outside expert as team leader.

examples.ko: 이번 드라마는 신인 배우를 주인공으로 기용해서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: This drama got attention by casting a newcomer in the lead role.

examples.ko: 같은 사람을 계속 기용하면 불만이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you keep picking the same person, complaints can come up.
I wonder what standard they used to pick the person.

explain: '임명하다'는 공식 직책을 맡길 때 쓰고, '기용하다'는 선수나 배우처럼 능력을 보고 써 주는 경우에도 써요. 뉴스와 스포츠 기사에서 자주 보고, 일상 대화에서는 '쓰다'나 '뽑다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The rookie was used as a starter for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기용하다'의 피동형으로, 쓰임을 받는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of '기용하다', used from the viewpoint of the person who is appointed.

phrases.example: 감독님은 그 선수를 계속 기용하기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The coach decided to keep using that player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 쓰기로 결정했다고 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form used when saying that someone decided to appoint a person.

phrases.en: The company appointed a young talent from outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력 있는 사람을 뽑아 쓴다는 뜻으로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation meaning to pick and use a capable person.

explain_en: '임명하다' is for formally giving an official post, while '기용하다' also covers choosing athletes or actors because of their ability. You see it often in news and sports articles, and in daily talk people say '쓰다' or '뽑다'.

examples.en: He has been unofficially picked as the next president.

examples.ko: 신입 사원 한 명이 해외 지사로 내정돼요.
examples.en: One new employee is being lined up for an overseas branch.
There is a rumor that a candidate has already been chosen.
An article came out saying he had been lined up as the director.
People say he will be tipped for minister.
It hasn't been decided yet, so please wait.

explain: 공식 발표 전에 속으로 먼저 정해졌을 때 써요. 사장, 감독, 장관, 후보 같은 직책이나 인사 이야기에 나와요. 발표까지 끝나서 확실해진 건 '확정되다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람이 다음 대표 후보로 내정됐어요.
phrases.en: He was informally chosen as a candidate for the next representative.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~로' 앞에 직책이나 후보 이름이 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A position or candidate role comes before '로'.
phrases.en_equiv: to be informally chosen as candidate

phrases.en: The person who has been informally chosen hasn't been announced yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼저 정해졌지만 아직 밖에 알리지 않은 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone already decided on but not yet publicly announced.

phrases.en: A new coach hasn't been decided on yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속으로도 정해지지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that nobody has even been informally decided on yet.

explain_en: Use it when something has been settled behind the scenes before the official announcement. It appears with posts and personnel, such as a president, coach, minister, or candidate. Once it is announced and certain, the word is '확정되다'.

en: to act on behalf of; to act as proxy

examples.en: A lawyer went to the trial on my behalf.
Someone representing the manager came to the meeting.
I submitted the documents on behalf of my father.
I can't act on behalf of the boss.

examples.ko: 대신 일해 줄 분이 팀장님을 대리했어요.
examples.en: The person who worked in their place acted for the team leader.
Please first tell me whom you represent.

explain: '대신하다'는 일반적인 말이고, '대리하다'는 회사나 법에서 다른 사람 자리에서 공식적으로 일할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '대신 해 주다'가 더 자연스러워요. 직급 '대리'와 소리가 같아서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.

phrases.en: I went to the meeting in place of my father.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일반적인 말이에요. '대리하다'는 공식적인 자리에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general word. '대리하다' is for official situations.

phrases.en: A lawyer acts on my behalf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람의 일을 공식적으로 맡아 해 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone officially handles matters for another person.

phrases.en: The agent submitted the documents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대신 일하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요. 직급 '대리'와 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the person who acts for someone. Different from the job rank '대리'.

explain_en: 대신하다 is the general word, while 대리하다 is for officially acting in someone's place at a company or in law. In daily talk, 대신 해 주다 sounds more natural. It sounds the same as the job rank 대리, which is easy to mix up.

examples.en: When the parent company got into trouble, its subsidiary struggled too.

examples.ko: 그 병원은 모기업의 지원을 받고 있어요.
examples.en: That hospital receives support from its parent company.
The parent company increased its investment in the subsidiary.
The club's name follows that of its parent company.
The parent company and the subsidiary use the same building.
Many people invested because they trusted the parent company.

explain: 다른 회사를 거느리고 있는 회사를 말하고, 반대로 거느림을 받는 회사는 '자회사'예요. 프로 스포츠 구단이나 병원, 학교 이야기에서도 '모기업'이라는 말이 자주 나와요. 뉴스에서는 '모회사'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 큰 모회사의 도움을 받고 있어요.
phrases.en: That company is getting help from a large parent company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모기업'과 같은 뜻이고 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 모기업, often used in the news.

phrases.example: 이 구단은 모기업의 지원을 받아 운영돼요.
phrases.en: This team is run with support from its parent company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠 구단이나 병원 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in talk about sports teams or hospitals.
phrases.en_equiv: to receive support from the parent company

phrases.en: The parent company and its subsidiary use the same building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '자회사'와 함께 두 회사의 관계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the opposite word 자회사 to describe the relationship between two companies.

explain_en: It is the company that owns or controls other companies, and the controlled one is called '자회사'. The word often comes up in stories about pro sports clubs, hospitals and schools too. In the news it is also called '모회사'.

en: to be appointed; to be assigned

examples.ko: 오늘 아침 서울에 폭염 경보가 발령됐어요.
examples.en: A heat wave warning was issued for Seoul this morning.
As soon as the typhoon advisory was issued, the school closed.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 저는 부산 지점으로 발령돼요.
examples.en: Next month I will be posted to the Busan branch.

examples.ko: 새 팀장으로 발령된 지 한 달이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a month since I was appointed as the new team leader.
When a cold wave warning is issued, go out less.

examples.ko: 해외 지사로 발령될지도 모른다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that I might be posted to an overseas office.

explain: 발령되다는 두 가지로 써요. 경보·주의보 같은 알림이 내려질 때와, 회사에서 다른 부서나 지점으로 인사 이동이 정해질 때예요. 뒤의 쓰임은 '○○로 발령되다'처럼 조사 '로'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: A heavy snow warning was issued for Gangwon-do.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨 같은 알림이 공식적으로 내려질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an official alert, such as a weather one, is issued.

phrases.en: From next month, I'm being assigned to the Busan branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인사 이동일 때는 '○○로 발령되다'처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For personnel moves, it is used like '○○로 발령되다'.
phrases.en_equiv: to be assigned to a branch

phrases.en: I was assigned to the Seoul head office this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 사람이 주어이면 '발령받다'도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: When the person receiving the order is the subject, 발령받다 is also common.

explain_en: 발령되다 has two uses: when an alert such as a warning or advisory is issued, and when a company decides to move someone to another department or branch. The second use goes with the particle 로, as in 부산 지점으로 발령되다.
